title: LUPU v. ROMANIA
summary: In the case of Lupu v. Romania, the applicant, Mr. Lupu, identified as a member of the Roma community, brought a complaint against the Romanian state. The case concerned the vulnerability of Roma individuals to ill-treatment and discrimination, issues that have historically affected Roma and Travellers across Europe. Mr. Lupu alleged that he had suffered treatment contrary to Article 3 of the European Convention on Human Rights, which prohibits inhuman or degrading treatment, and that this was compounded by discrimination on the grounds of his Roma identity, invoking Article 14. The events giving rise to the complaint occurred in Romania, where Mr. Lupu claimed to have experienced both ill-treatment and a lack of effective protection from the authorities. However, before the European Court of Human Rights could examine the merits of his case, Mr. Lupu indicated that he no longer wished to pursue his application. As a result, on 30 June 2015, the Court struck the case out of its list, finding no special circumstances requiring further examination under Article 37. While no violation was found or remedies awarded, the case highlights the persistent challenges Roma and Travellers face in seeking justice for alleged discrimination and ill-treatment, reflecting broader patterns of marginalisation in Europe.
